question: A Team account with fifteen members has just had the Gmail connector enabled by the Primary Owner. How does each member gain access through the connector?
options: A) One member authenticates once, granting Gmail access to the whole team.
B) The Primary Owner authenticates for everyone through a single shared service account.
C) Members share one OAuth token that IT distributes to the whole team.
D) Each member individually authenticates via OAuth with their own Google credentials.
correct_answers: D) Each member individually authenticates via OAuth with their own Google credentials.
explanations: Incorrect. Authentication is per-user; one member's OAuth grant does not extend to teammates' inboxes.
Incorrect. There is no shared service account model; each user connects their own Google account individually.
Incorrect. Shared or distributed tokens are not how the connector works; per-user authentication keeps data separate.
Correct. Even after org-level enablement, each user authenticates through standard OAuth with their own credentials, keeping access per-person.
